reading_notes: applies_from is the legal application date at UTC midnight. It is not a deadline for filing anything; it is the date the obligation begins to bind.
No tense is stored. Whether an obligation is in force depends on when you are reading, so compute it against applies_from rather than caching a status.
amended_by, where present, is the instrument that moved the date. Reading the founding regulation alone has already produced one published correction on this site.
Every entry cites the article that sets the date. If you cannot reach our conclusion from the linked source, treat that as a defect and tell us.
Absence from this corpus is not a statement that nothing applies. It is a short table that is right rather than a long one that is mostly right.

obligations.name: Prohibited AI practices and AI literacy
obligations.summary: Unacceptable-risk systems banned outright. Staff operating AI must be demonstrably competent to do so.

obligations.name: General-purpose AI obligations and penalties
obligations.summary: Model documentation, training-data summaries and copyright policy. The penalty regime becomes enforceable.

obligations.name: Article 50 transparency obligations
obligations.summary: AI systems must disclose that they are AI. Synthetic content must be marked machine-readable.
obligations.penalty: Up to EUR 15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover

obligations.name: High-risk obligations, Annex III
obligations.instrument: EU AI Act 2024/1689, as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
obligations.article: Art. 113, as amended — deferred from 2 August 2026
obligations.summary: Risk management, data governance, logging, human oversight and conformity assessment for listed high-risk uses. Deferred, not cancelled.

obligations.name: AI Transparency Act
obligations.instrument: California SB 942, as amended by AB 853
obligations.summary: Generative systems with over one million monthly users must embed latent disclosure in what they generate, offer a manifest disclosure, and publish a free detection tool.

obligations.name: Hosting platforms and large online platforms
obligations.instrument: California SB 942, as amended by AB 853
obligations.summary: Platforms hosting generative systems, and large online platforms distributing their output, take on their own disclosure and provenance duties.

obligations.name: Article 50(2) marking for systems already on the market
obligations.instrument: EU AI Act 2024/1689, as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
obligations.article: Art. 50(2), four-month transitional period — Reg. 2026/1744 recital 38
obligations.summary: Generative systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 were given four months of relief from the machine-readable marking duty. That relief expires and marking becomes mandatory. Systems placed on the market on or after 2 August 2026 never had it.

obligations.name: High-risk obligations, Annex I products
obligations.instrument: EU AI Act 2024/1689, as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
obligations.article: Art. 6(1), as amended — deferred from 2 August 2027
obligations.summary: AI acting as a safety component of a regulated product falls under the full high-risk regime.

obligations.name: Legacy general-purpose models
obligations.summary: Models already on the market before August 2025 lose their grace period and must comply in full.
